rows.proof_boundary: The prime number theorem supplies convergence and r_1=0.
rows.statement: For 0<alpha<1, set r_k=sum_(n>=k)mu(n)/n, M(k)=sum_(n<=k)mu(n), B_alpha=sum k^(-alpha)|r_k|^2, and M_alpha=sum M(k)^2/k^(2+alpha).

rows.proof_boundary: Classical input only; it supplies no RH-strength power saving.
rows.statement: The prime number theorem gives sum_(n>=1)mu(n)/n=0 and M(N)/N->0.

rows.proof_boundary: Immediate from the reciprocal-Mobius tail definition.
rows.statement: r_k-r_(k+1)=mu(k)/k.

rows.proof_boundary: Telescope sum n(r_n-r_(n+1)); H is the prefix Hardy operator.
rows.statement: M(k)=sum_(n=1)^k r_n-k*r_(k+1), hence M(k)/k=H(r)(k)-r_(k+1).

rows.proof_boundary: Abel summation and M(N)/N->0.
A nonsharp explicit Schur-test form of the weighted Hardy inequality; no Mobius cancellation is used.
rows.statement: On l2(k^(-alpha)), H has norm at most h_alpha=sqrt(2(3+alpha))/(1+alpha).

rows.proof_boundary: A nonsharp explicit Schur-test form of the weighted Copson inequality; the constant blows up as alpha->1.
rows.statement: The tail operator Cb(k)=sum_(n>=k)b_n/n has norm at most c_alpha=sqrt(2(3-alpha))/(1-alpha) on l2(k^(-alpha)).

rows.proof_boundary: Combine rows 4-7 with the one-step weighted shift bounds.
rows.statement: M_alpha^(1/2)<=(h_alpha+2^(alpha/2))B_alpha^(1/2) and B_alpha^(1/2)<=(1+c_alpha)M_alpha^(1/2).

rows.proof_boundary: Concavity and 1-alpha<=2^(-alpha); valid for every k>=1.
rows.statement: For w_(alpha,k)=k^(1-alpha)-(k-1)^(1-alpha), (1-alpha)k^(-alpha)<=w_(alpha,k)<=k^(-alpha).

rows.proof_boundary: Rows 8 and 9 give explicit two-sided norm constants.
rows.statement: The limiting OU tail energy sum w_(alpha,k)|r_k|^2 is finite iff M_alpha is finite.

rows.proof_boundary: M(x)=M(k) on each half-open cell [k,k+1).
rows.statement: I_alpha=integral_1^infinity M(x)^2*x^(-2-alpha)dx equals (1/(1+alpha))*sum M(k)^2*[k^(-1-alpha)-(k+1)^(-1-alpha)].

rows.proof_boundary: Bound x^(-2-alpha) above and below on each unit cell.
rows.statement: 2^(-2-alpha)M_alpha<=I_alpha<=M_alpha.

rows.proof_boundary: Classical Abel/Mellin identity for the Mertens function.
rows.statement: 1/zeta(s)=s*integral_1^infinity M(x)x^(-s-1)dx initially for Re(s)>1.

rows.proof_boundary: Mellin-Plancherel plus analytic continuation from Re(s)>1; finiteness rules out a boundary pole.
rows.statement: If I_alpha<infinity and beta=(1+alpha)/2, then I_alpha=(1/(2pi))*integral_R dt/[(beta^2+t^2)|zeta(beta+it)|^2].

rows.proof_boundary: Compare k with 2^j on each dyadic block.
rows.statement: For D_j=2^(-2j)sum_(2^j<=k<2^(j+1))M(k)^2, 2^(-2-alpha)sum 2^(-alpha*j)D_j<=M_alpha<=sum 2^(-alpha*j)D_j.

rows.proof_boundary: Root test for the nonnegative generating series sum 2^(-alpha*j)D_j.
rows.statement: M_alpha<infinity for every alpha>0 iff limsup_(j->infinity)D_j^(1/j)<=1.

rows.proof_boundary: Rows 10, 15, and 16 composed with the cofinal OU criterion; this records an equivalent antecedent, not its proof.
rows.statement: RH iff for every epsilon>0, sum_(K<=k<2K)M(k)^2=O_epsilon(K^(2+epsilon)) on dyadic K.

rows.proof_boundary: Expand M(k)^2 and count the k containing each ordered pair.
rows.statement: sum_(k<=X)M(k)^2=sum_(n<=X)mu(n)^2(X-n+1)+2sum_(h<X)sum_(m<=X-h)mu(m)mu(m+h)(X-m-h+1).

rows.proof_boundary: Reverse the m,Y summations exactly.
rows.statement: With C_h(Y)=sum_(m<=Y)mu(m)mu(m+h), the off-diagonal in row 18 equals 2sum_(h<X)sum_(Y<=X-h)C_h(Y).

rows.proof_boundary: Rows 17-19; the correlation sum is signed and anchored at m=1.
rows.statement: The dyadic RH criterion is equivalent to sum_(h<X)sum_(Y<=X-h)C_h(Y)=O_epsilon(X^(2+epsilon)); the squarefree diagonal is O(X^2).

rows.proof_boundary: The same divergent scale as the absolute OU and remainder bounds; a generic sequence inequality cannot close RH.
rows.statement: Generic weighted Hardy applied to M(k)=sum_(n<=k)mu(n) costs sum_(n<=N)mu(n)^2*n^(-alpha), of order N^(1-alpha).

rows.proof_boundary: Published averaged-Chowla input only; no anchored cumulative Mertens estimate is attributed to that theorem.
rows.statement: Matomaki-Radziwill-Tao prove an o(H^k X) average over all shift k-tuples, and state that the result also holds for mu.

rows.proof_boundary: Blocks promotion of averaged or logarithmically averaged Chowla into the required origin-anchored cumulative theorem.
rows.statement: The published theorem averages every base shift, whereas C_h(Y) fixes the origin; even an anchored terminal bound sum_h|C_h(Y)|=o(Y^2), integrated naively in Y, has cubic rather than X^(2+epsilon) scale.

rows.proof_boundary: An exceptional anchored slice can carry the RH-strength obligation even when its density among shifts tends to zero.
rows.statement: Almost-all short-interval cancellation leaves the single prefix M(X) and the h_1=0 correlation slice uncontrolled.

rows.proof_boundary: This is RH-equivalent. No OU bound, full Burnol bound, RH, PF-infinity, or Lambda<=0 conclusion is recorded.
rows.statement: Prove D_j=2^(o(j)), equivalently the dyadic Mertens mean-square or signed anchored integrated-correlation bound, without assuming a zero-free half-plane or RH.

status: exact OU-tail/Mertens/dyadic/anchored-correlation reduction with one open RH-equivalent mean-square gate
